fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Trim back dense vegetation along the driveway to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles approaching the main residence.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to create a clear gap between plants and the buildings.
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles blocking the path between the driveway and the main residence.
• Mark or label any gate in the perimeter fencing that provides the most direct access to the rear of the property.
• Keep rear-access gates unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock so responders can reach the detached structure without delay.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without obstruction.
• Clear a walking path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front to the rear for responders on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house, garage, or any outbuildings.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open gaps between the remaining trees.
• Remove shrubs and small plants growing directly against the exterior walls of the house.
• Clear grass and low ground cover within several feet of the foundation and any outbuildings.
• Separate tree canopies from nearby shrubs so fire cannot climb from low plants up into the trees next to the house.
• Remove dead grass, dry leaves, and fallen branches that have collected under trees near the structure.
• Thin scattered trees on the approach to the house so the driveway stays open and visible from both directions.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches from the road to the house.
• Cut back any vegetation along the driveway edges that narrows the travel lane or blocks sightlines.
• Move any woodpiles, lumber, or stored materials away from the exterior walls of the house.
• Mow grass across the property regularly to keep it short, especially in areas close to the house and driveway.
